overview: Saichania (meaning 'beautiful' in Mongolian) was a large, heavily armoured ankylosaur from the Late Cretaceous of Mongolia and China, living approximately 80 million years ago (Campanian). Named by Maryańska in 1977, it reached an estimated 6.6 metres in length and is known from the Baruungoyot Formation of Omnogov province, Mongolia, and from probable occurrences in China. It was one of the most heavily armoured ankylosaurs known, with extensive dorsal and lateral body armour and a tail club.

Saichania belongs to Ankylosaurinae within Ankylosauridae and is closely related to Tarchia from the slightly younger Nemegt Formation. Its well-preserved material, including partial skulls and body armour, has made it a key reference for understanding Asian ankylosaur anatomy. Unlike the drier Djadokhta fauna of Pinacosaurus, Saichania may have inhabited more arid dune environments based on its depositional context in the Baruungoyot Formation.

articles.title: Discovery and Naming
articles.body: Saichania chulsanensis was described by Polish palaeontologist Teresa Maryańska in 1977 from material collected during Polish-Mongolian expeditions to the Gobi Desert. The genus name, meaning 'beautiful' in Mongolian, was chosen to reflect the quality of preservation of the specimens. The species name refers to the Khulsan (Chulsan) locality.

articles.title: Armour and Defence
articles.body: Saichania possessed some of the most extensive body armour known among ankylosaurs, with large flat osteoderms on the back, smaller ossicles between them, and spines projecting from the shoulders and flanks. The broad, low body and well-ossified eyelids suggest a strongly defensive lifestyle. Its tail club would have been a powerful weapon against large predators such as Tarbosaurus.

articles.title: Skull and Nasal Passages
articles.body: The skull of Saichania shows complex nasal passages that looped back on themselves—more elaborate than those of some other ankylosaurs. These tortuous airways may have helped warm and humidify inhaled air in the dry, dusty Cretaceous desert environment, or may have played a role in thermoregulation or olfaction.

articles.title: Comparison with Tarchia
articles.body: Saichania and Tarchia are closely related Mongolian ankylosaurids. Tarchia, from the overlying Nemegt Formation, was named by Maryańska in 1977 from a specimen with a notably large braincase. The two genera co-define a distinctively Mongolian Late Cretaceous ankylosaur assemblage distinct from the North American ankylosaurid fauna.

record.mya: late Campanian, about 75-72 million years ago
record.description: Saichania chulsanensis was an ankylosaurid from the Baruungoyot Formation of Mongolia, based on a skull and partial associated skeleton with additional referred material.
facts: The holotype preserves an excellent skull, neck armour, vertebrae, girdles and forelimbs but not a complete body.
Some mounted or referred specimens have been questioned or reassigned, so tail and hindquarter anatomy must be labelled by specimen.

review.ageReviewNote: The type is late Campanian Baruungoyot Formation; an isolated 80 Ma point is not justified.
